utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Before we continue with your witness, Mr. Behar, I see that Mr. Stamp is here and we have received his e-mail of last evening. We're grateful for that, Mr. Stamp, and for the information you've conveyed. Let us hope that things progress as planned. The Chamber would indicate that it is aware of informal approaches from counsel as to the position on Friday of next week. The Chamber's position had been that we would sit on Friday unless we were able to get through the witnesses earlier, and we are encouraged, particularly in view of the fact that the two witnesses you're now going to call, one is a 92 bis and one a 92 ter, their subject matter ought to make them shorter witnesses than the witnesses originally listed. So with that encouragement, we would take the decision this morning not to sit on the Friday in the expectation that it will be possible to finish the listed witnesses by Wednesday. So I hope that assists with your planning and certainly with the planning that counsel for the accused has been having, but it does mean that the Chamber will be conscious of time to finish this week's witnesses this week and so that there'll be three clear days to deal with the witnesses next week. Is there any news on the third witness for next week, Mr. Stamp, at this stage?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Not anything confirmed. We are trying our best to -- to ensure that the Court uses the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You encourage us to leave it in safe hands. Is that it, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Very well. We look forward to learning about that, and I hope counsel will work together consistently with their obligations to try and ensure that we can finish the witnesses by the end of the sitting on Wednesday of next week, but the decision of the Chamber will now be firm that we will not sit on the Friday of next week. So that, I hope, is clear for everybody. Thank you very much, Mr. Stamp. Mr. Behar -- Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. The Defence will make its contribution to the realisation of your plans and your decisions, but I would like to note one thing. I would like the Prosecution to promptly advise us about the order of the witnesses, because it's very important for your preparations. The -- we don't know whether a witness will testify -- come to testify on Wednesday or Monday. It's very important for us to know that. So I would just like to make this request. So by close of business on Friday, we be given the exact order of witnesses so that we could prepare and so that your decision could be complied with. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I'm sure Mr. Stamp will realise that both the Chamber and you are anxious to know that, but I'm sure much depends upon the third witness next week that is yet subject to discussion. So we do know that two witnesses that have been identified will replace K86 and K79 in that order, as I understand it, but there's the question of the third witness yet to be resolved. Thank you very much. Mr. Behar, at last you become centre stage.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Your Honours. With the Court's permission there are a couple of very brief issues that I would request to revisit with the witness, and with the Court's leave I will be brief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Behar has one or two final questions for you. Mr. Behar.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Good morning, sir. I asked you yesterday about the time that you were hiding in the fields between Celine and Bela Crkva.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Could I have Exhibit P00650 on the screen, please, from yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Sir, you indicated that this photo was taken in the spring. Can you tell us, was it taken during that period, I believe you described it as a 30-day period when you were hiding in the fields and then finding and burying the massacred people?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And are you able to provide a more specific or a more exact date for when the photo was taken?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It could have been around 5 April.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And is there anything specific that makes you think it would have been the 5th of April?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The reason is because I know the -- when I was positioned in this place. We did not stay at the same place all the time. We always tried to fight -- to find the safest place for us to be.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: If I could next have Exhibit P00651, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Sir, yesterday you described - the reference is at page 86, line 24 - that this photograph was taken during a time when you were away from the village and had gone to a location where the whole population was gathered after the 25th of March. To begin with, are you able to provide a more specific day for when this photograph was taken?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This photograph was taken about seven days after the population left the village, after the 28th of March. So the date could be around the 7th of April, 6th or 7th of April.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And your answer yesterday was recorded as saying that you'd gone to a location where the whole population was gathered after the 25th of March. Can you explain what you mentioned -- pardon me, what you meant by that and who assembled there?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were not there when the population gathered, because the -- we did not have any contact with the whole population. The population started to move there on the 25th and the 26th of March. Then the population were forcibly removed from that area and directed towards Albania. I was in Zrze at the time, about seven kilometres from Celine.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: So am I understanding right, then, that you were not in the same place as the population that you were described -- or that you've just described?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We visited the place during the other days, but on the 25th and 26th we were not there. On the 28th the population was removed from Celina and was directed towards Albania.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: I see. I think that clears it up for me, sir. Thank you. Those are my questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Djurdjic, do you cross-examine?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Jemini. My name is Veljko Djurdjic. I'm a member of the Defence team of the accused Vlastimir Djordjevic. Here with me is Ms. Mary O'Leary, who is also a member of our Defence team. I have some questions for you regarding the statements that you've given so far, and in light of the fact that you've been here before to testify, you know that I have to ask you to wait for my question to be interpreted and then provide your answer. And I would also like you to listen carefully to my questions in order to be able to give us brief and accurate and precise answers.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, I would like to have P650 on our screens, or in fact, we can keep the 651 on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: You told us yesterday that had population had gathered there, and this is a photograph of you sitting here. Is this the group that always came into the village every evening?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I see that you're lying down here. Were you not afraid of the Serbian forces?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the moment when the NATO intervention occurred during the day, and only during that time we felt safe and secure. The Serb forces at that time were not active.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And will you tell me how the NATO alliance intervened on that day?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you know, of course, about the NATO air-strikes. When the NATO planes were flying over the area, the Serb forces sheltered somewhere else, and we felt safe during that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. But you remember that when this photograph was taken that there was a NATO action on that day. That's what you told us, and that's what I'm asking you. Do you know where this action took place?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not only that day but every day there were NATO air-strikes. And every day during those air-strikes we felt safe. Every time that the NATO planes were not heard, we did not feel safe and we took shelter. However, I don't know what the targets of the NATO air-strikes were at the time, but we could hear that they were flying.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, but I note from your statements that you have no problems with your eyesight or your hearing, but -- so did you notice the bombing of Nogavac at that time, for instance?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now tell me, was there anyone who was on guard duty who is not on this picture, for instance?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The whole group is here lying down. There was another group who took shelter somewhere else. We did not stay, all of us, together for security reasons. We, however, would observe and keep watch in order to see whether the Serb forces were coming towards where we were staying. We did not have a guard when we were here in the photograph. We were not a group that was armed or organised or anything like that. We just helped the population.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Well, how did you help?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 28th March, in the evening, we went by chance to this place that you see here from Zrze and Bellacerke, and that was the time when the population was ordered to go towards Albania. And, by chance, we met the population here, and we tried to help the villagers as much as we could. I led the group. The first thing was to separate the dead from the living so that we could help the living and not let them be massacred again. Another thing was to visit the whole village and identify all the people who had been massacred and killed in the village. This we did on the Sunday. Then we also buried the bodies so that the enemy would not take them away from the village. This we did. We buried all of them except the five people from my family who were taken by the forces. And we tried to protect the village and the villagers as much as we could. We couldn't do much, of course, but this is what we did during those two months.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Jemini, but as far as I can see, you're all laughing in this photograph.

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Wherever there is grief, there is laughter as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. But could you tell me, those tractors, and I can't see what it is there above your head, I'm not sure if it's you, is it a truck, the rear end of the truck?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a tractor covered with a plastic sheet. This is where the population were sheltering up to this moment. Then the cars and the tractors and everything were left there, and the population had to walk the whole distance towards Albania, about 50 kilometres. So what you see here is a tractor covered with a plastic sheet to protect from the rain.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do I understand you rightly that you say that this is the 28th of March, that this is the date when this photograph was taken?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No. This photograph was taken around the 7th or 8th of April. The tractors and equipment remained there till the day the population came back. Some of the cars and the equipment were looted by the police and the people who helped them.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could I please -- okay. Anyway, it's the same picture. When you were shown Exhibit 650 and when my learned colleague Behar asked you, you said that you switched -- that you changed places all time to time, that you moved from one place to another and that was the explanation for the photograph. Why did you do that?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: We moved because the police would come sometimes very close to the positions we were. They came very close to this place that you see in the photograph, because they looted some of the cars and the trucks and the tractors. These were the first days when we were there. On the other days we went there only during the evening or at night. During the day we stayed in safer places.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. But why were you fleeing from the police?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think this is a logical question. They killed every living person that they saw, so how could you think we would stay there and not flee from the police? They exterminated everybody from the territory in the whole area between Gjakova and the plain. Everybody was expelled or killed. We were the only ones, the 15 or 16 of us, we were the only ones that remained in that area, on the plain, during that period. And we would have died if they met us. They had no mercy.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You mentioned Djakovica. How do you know that they were expelling people from Djakovica?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The positions where we are here in this photograph is a vantage point, and from there you can see Gjakova, Ura e Shi --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Correction: Ura e Shenjte.

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: And from that position we could see the expulsion of the population from Gjakova and Mitrovica. Every evening we met people that were leaving their homes, and that's where we got our information from, but we could also observe their movements.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did I understand you correctly that you mentioned Mitrovica?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mitrovica is very far. It's on the other side. But the population of Mitrovica passed by the area of Celine and Krusha e Madhe when they were directed towards Albania during the NATO intervention.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you agree with me when I say that Celine is halfway between Prizren and Djakovica, roughly speaking?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Roughly. You would be right.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And to Prizren and to Djakovica it's about 35 kilometres?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: From Prizren to Celine there are approximately 17 kilometres, whereas from Celine to Gjakove approximately the same distance, 17 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Yes, quite right. It's about 80 to Pec. Now, tell me, please, weren't you afraid of becoming mixed up with the population who was going from Djakovica towards Prizren? You talked to them. You were in contact with them.

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were 2 or 3 kilometres far from the asphalt road, the main road Gjakove-Prizren. Therefore, there was no reason for us to be afraid. These people were escorted by the police forces on their way to Albania, so we had no contact whatsoever with them. We did have a contact with a person who was removed from the convoy, who left the convoy. We met him in the evening, but he was not -- he had -- he had fainted. He lost consciousness, and after he recovered he continued his way to Albania.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, would you agree with me that all these people on the picture were military-able men?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Jemini, are you from Celine originally, your family? Does it hail from there?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. What was your grandfather's profession?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was a farmer.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And what about your father?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Farmer.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And how many uncles did you have on your father's side?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: One.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Was he a farmer too?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he worked at the railway station, but at this time he was retired.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Was your grandfather alive in 1999?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I don't remember my grandfather. He had died before I was born.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. After your grandfather's death did the sons separate or did they carry on with their communal living?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: They carried on with their communal living for a while, and in 1970 the sons separated. So my father with his children and my uncle with his children started to live separately.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. From your statements I have drawn the conclusion that on your family property or compound that the compound was in fact made up of five houses. Am I right in thinking that?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, all these houses, did they belong to your father and you?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: These houses belonged to my father and myself and my brothers. We are four sons.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, the four of you, you four sons, were you separate from your father?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we were together.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you tell me what the surface area was of your compound, including the family houses? What area would that be? How much land?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: 0.6 hectares.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, around your compound was there a wall? Was there a wall which separated the street and other yards and compounds from your own?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And what was the wall made of?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Concrete bricks, 40 by 20.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And could you tell me how high the wall was?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Two twenty to 250 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, was there an entrance gate to your compound?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And what was the width of that gate?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: About 4 to 5 wide and about 3.5 metres tall.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Djurdjic, the transcript correctly records what was said, but I think you and I understood the fence height to be 2.2 or 2 metres 20 and 2 metres 50, whereas what is recorded is 250 metres. It's a very high wall.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Yes. Now you've drawn my attention to that, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jemini, let's repeat for the transcript. How high was your wall, the wall around your compound?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Between 2.20 and 2.50 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you, yes. Now, the gate, the entrance gate, what was that made of?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Wood.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, is that customary? Is it usual that at night in the families and their compounds the gate is kept shut?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Usually, yes, but there are also cases when the gate is kept open.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. As far as I was able to understand from your statements, two houses were completely finished, whereas the other houses, the three other houses, were still under construction. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think, yes. You could live in two of them, and in three of them nobody lived.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Your family comprised of four brothers and your father. Did you all live in the same building, in the same house, or did you use the different premises?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: We all lived in the same house.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And the other one was for guests; right?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, for guests, and I had also my office there, my library.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. If I understood you correctly, Isuf Jemini did not live together with you on your -- in your family compound.

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. As we're talking about him, how come he happened to be with you on the 25th?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not only on the 25th, but even the time before that as we are cousins, and since there's only one wall dividing the two houses, our houses are very close to each other. During the time of the 24th and 25th of March, not only with my cousin but with all other family members and other villagers we stayed together.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And why were you all together?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because we were afraid. We were anticipating the Serb forces to enter the village. That's why we felt safer when we were staying together.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And how long were you together before this 25th?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Every evening we were together. When we would come after work we would stay together, but during that period for a month we were almost all the time together. We were discussing possibilities of leaving the place and going to Prizren for safety reasons.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And who were these others outside your family who were living with you for that month that you say?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The members of my family, the members of my uncle's family, other relatives. We would stay together either in my house or in my uncle's house. The women, the children, and the elderly were really scared, and that's why we kind of felt responsible for them.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And were there -- were they members of the broader Jemini family?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And did they live in Celine otherwise?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And where is Isuf's house -- or, rather, his family land and his compound? Compared to where yours was, where was his located?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: About 15 metres away from our house. Isuf's house was about 15 metres away from the house we lived in.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So do I understand it that he had another gateway into his compound but that otherwise you were next-door neighbours?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but there was another entrance between our houses, a communicating door between the two properties.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Jemini, you graduated from the -- from the technical engineering faculty, if I'm not mistaken; right?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And you were a student at the Pristina university, right?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And when did you graduate?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Were you a student in 1981?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And did you take part in the student demonstrations of 1981?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us the reason for the demonstrations?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were many reasons for the demonstrations of political and economic nature, and all these reasons brought to that war.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And what were the demonstration -- what were the demonstrators calling for? What did they want?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were calling for freedom, democracy, and other demands which I cannot remember all of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And what about Kosovo republic? Was that one of the demands they were making?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It was too early to demand that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You were a freshman that year, were you not?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I enrolled in 1979. You know that the technical engineering faculty takes you five years to complete it. So I started in 1979. I was not a freshman that year.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And did you take part, perhaps, in the Kacanik Assembly, Kacanicka Skupstina?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And when the multi-party system was introduced, were you perhaps a member of some political party? And that was in 1991, I believe.

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Democratic Alliance of Kosova. The LDK. It was the only Albanian party in Kosova until the period after the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, not the only one, but you say you were a member of that political party. Right. Now, tell me, were you just a member or did you hold a post within the party?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was a leader of this party branch for the village, and at the time I was also the mayor of the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Well, you asked the question before me. What year did you become a leader in the village?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And at the age of 25 you were a leader to your father and everyone else, all the other elders of the families in Celine.

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was an accomplishment for the village, to have an educated and schooled people to lead them. From 1986 until two months ago, I led the village. There were other persons who had graduated from faculties coming from Celine, too. Hashim Rexhepi is one of them. So the entire leadership of the village now comprises of educated young men who have graduated from various faculties.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, but I know many people from that region who graduated before you, before 1986, but what I wanted to ask you was something else. How were you elected the elder?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are many educated persons in many places, but just one is elected the elder. My work, my activities, my honesty made the villagers vote for me and elect me as their elder. There was not much of a perspective for me. I wished I had a different perspective, but at least I did give my contribution in developing the village without any personal gains. I did give my personal contribution, as did my family, to develop and achieve a progress in the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And if I understood you correctly, that was at the elections. It was at the elections that you were elected village leader.

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course, that was at the election, as was in other areas of Kosova. It's not that one was elected based on the will of a certain group; it was the people who elected their leaders.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And who organised the elections?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The leadership of Kosova always organised the elections. From 1986 until 1990, the organs of the Kosova leadership comprising of Serbs and Albanians organised that, and afterwards, after the 1990s, the elections were organised as it is in other states, every four years when the population casts their vote and elects their leaders.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, I don't quite understand now. Was it elections for president of the local commune? Is that what you mean?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course, local elections in the villages and communes, municipalities.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, if you hadn't met him before, I'm sure you've met Selihi Halim now, and he said that there never was a village leader nor did he ever take part in some Assembly organised to elect a leader.

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what Salihi said. Salihi was one of the villagers in a village made up of 2.000 inhabitants. Maybe he didn't vote, he didn't take part in the election; however, I should think he knows that -- how the election process is carried out.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let me ask you this: Was Celine with the Mala Hoca, Nogavac, and Krusa part of the same local commune?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We did not get the name of the local commune.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Celine belonged to the municipality of Rahovec. Rahovec is the township that includes 22 villages, Celine, Nagavc, and Krusha e Madhe were one local community -- considered as one local community.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And did you perhaps know Ekrem Rexha?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've heard the name. I don't know him personally.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And did you hear about some instructions in February 1999 that related to administrative affairs issued by Mr. Rexha?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Mr. Jemini, could you please describe where your family farm or property is in the village?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Our family compound is in a very important part of the village. It's about 700 metres from the main road at the place where there is a turn off road that goes to Bellacerke, Krusha e Madhe, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Am I right when I say that the road that you mentioned, the Prizren-Djakovica road, is south of the village of Celine?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The main road, the Prizren-Gjakove road, is an asphalt road. It's in the upper part of the village. To the east of the road is the Celine village. You can find the Celine village and my house as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You mention that you can go both to Velika Krusa and to Bela Crkva through Celine. Am I right if I say that those are the places that are at the opposite ends of the road in relation to Celine?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand the question. Could you repeat it, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Let me be more specific. When you enter the village of Celine from the main road, then you take different roads to Bela Crkva and Velika Krusa. There are two different roads?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The main road goes towards Celine, but then there is a junction where the road separates. One direction goes towards Krusha e Madhe, the other to Bellacerke. When you turn right you go to Krusa, and when you turn left you go to Bellacerke. It's the same road going to these two places.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And this intersection now, in relation to this intersection where the road veers off towards Velika Krusa, where is your house?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right at that intersection. Sixty metres before you get to the -- to the junction or intersection.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] To speed things up, could I please get a Defence document up on the screen? That's D002-5633.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jemini, I think that you could tell us -- or, rather, can you tell us on the basis of this photograph where the Prizren-Djakovica road is? Just a moment. Wait for a little while for the usher to provide you with the pen. Can you see the road?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The photograph is not very clear. If Celine is here -- I'm not sure where Gjakove-Prizren road is. Celine is here. Then this should be the Prizren-Gjakove road, but I'm not really clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We have a better photograph for that. Now, this is the village of Celine. Could you please mark your house.

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you could zoom in, please, because I cannot see properly.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Well, as far as I can understand, we can't do it on this photograph. Could I then please have photograph D002-5635 -- or, rather, I would just like to ask the usher to scroll the photograph down a little bit and then to zoom on the village itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the little dot that's been put on this photograph is really not essential, so we can risk losing it. This is not an exhibit of any sort. So we can lose it. Can we just scroll down -- or, rather, up a little bit and then to focus or to zoom in on Celine. I don't know if you can do it. Yes, on this part.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Witness, sir, can we do something now? I know that it's difficult because this is an image taken from space. Can you find your way around, get your bearings here?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The blue point marking Celine is the Celine village. Just on that point there or is it the wider area with the point in the middle?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Sir, this is supposed to be an aerial photograph of the village of Celine and the area around it. Now, if you recognise some buildings or roads -- rather, I would like you to mark your family property on this photograph, and then the location of the school, the mosque, of the road to Velika Krusa, to Bela Crkva. Are you able to recognise all that?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'm just asking, is the whole area here the Celine village or not? I don't understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Witness, according to this map it is Celine, and it is indicated as such. To my mind it should be the centre of the village.

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Unfortunately, the photograph is not clear at all. When I gave testimony the other times, we did have very clear photographs that I could read. Here I cannot see where the Prizren-Gjakove road is.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I could ask the usher -- well, that's the next photograph. It's a map of Celine. It's D002-5635. Yes, but could you zoom out a little bit? And now I want to see all the roads. I think you can see all the roads.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Can you see the roads now, Mr. Jemini?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. If we start from the point A here where Celine is, the main road, Prizren-Gjakove, is here, should be here, but still I cannot see it clearly.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Now I would like to ask you -- well, I didn't see where you pointed, but could you please mark the road leading to Prizren and the road leading to Djakovica. Could you please mark the Prizren part of the road with the letters PZ and Djakovica DJ.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... see the main road. That's his problem.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Marks] On the basis of this photograph, I can minimally say that this is the Gjakove-Prizren road. However, I cannot see where you turn to enter the village. I cannot see the road that takes you from this road to the village because the photograph is not clear. As I said when I gave testimony in the other trials, the photographs were -- the photographs were much clearer than this one.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Yes, but we didn't have an image. We didn't have -- you had a map and this is an image. But let me ask you, this section where you put the letter P, and as you head towards the letters DJ, do you see an intersection where a road leads uphill and one leads towards the left-hand side and one leads to where you put the letter I? Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here where I marked?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Well, here where you put the dot.

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is the entrance to the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you mind marking this with number 1.

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you now, as you head down this road towards the village, could you please mark with an X the spot where the intersection we were talking about is located?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It must be here. Then the direction to Krusha is this one. Then on the opposite side you go to Bellacerke.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Just take it slowly. This section where you put the X, could you please mark it with number 2 also.

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: For the transcript, I would say that number 2 marks the intersection with the road leading to Bela Crkva and Velika Krusa. Now I would like you to put an arrow marking the direction for Bela Crkva.

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Well done. So B is Bela Crkva next to the arrow that marks the direction of Bela Crkva, and could you please put K to an arrow that will mark the direction of Velika Krusa.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Isn't that already done? He has marked two arrows in opposite directions, B toward the north and K toward the south.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Thank you. Yes. I was just actually describing for the transcript. That's why I was saying this. Otherwise, yes, of course you are right.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Witness, since this is an image taken from space and since it is a very broad image, now, could you tell us where the photograph that we were looking at, the one taken by the tractor, was taken? Can we see this spot on this image?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: If we accept that the point that marks Celine is the centre of the village, about one and a half to two kilometres from the centre is the place where we took the photograph. And this is the place where the whole population had gathered on the 28th.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I can see two dots here. Could you please make a circle, and then we can mark it with number 3.

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you now indicate, if you can see it, the location of your family property.

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right at the place where I marked with a number 2, where --

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: No, no. Please don't. Please don't. Don't go over it, because then we won't be able to see.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we -- could I please tender this photograph into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes. We will receive it, but it should be clear for the transcript, in our understanding, that the X with the number 2 by it is the intersection or the junction, and the house is just about on that junction. Now, that -- I see the witness is nodding agreement, so that it's clear. Yes, Mr. Djurdjic?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, well, I was not sure what the witness would mark here. I wanted now to reload the photograph and then to have him mark his house, the mosque, and the school as a new exhibit because it's a very small-scale image, and I was afraid that if the witness were to mark everything we wouldn't be able to actually discern anything. I didn't want to mar this exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will receive it, Mr. Djurdjic, and see whether you can get more detail, but I think you will agree it's a very difficult image for anybody to be working on as a witness.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be D00071, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Now I would like to ask the court deputy to reload the same photograph without any markings.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jemini, this is the same photograph. Could we please start with you putting a dot marking the location of your house? Just take it slowly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Can -- the scale is so small, Mr. Djurdjic. Do you think we should try to go in a little closer if you're wanting this sort of detail identified?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If it's possible, if the court deputy could do it, then I would kindly ask him to do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Well, is it better like this, Mr. Jemini?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's much better now.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Now, since you were able to look at it from a broader viewpoint, could you please just mark the place where your house is.

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said, I -- my house is very close to the intersection. This position that I marked here.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please put number 1, but please don't put it on the intersection of the roads.

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And now in relation to your house, where is the intersection that we were talking about a little while ago?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right here. The junction is right here. I can mark here where you turn. So this is where you enter, and this is where you turn, and the house is right there as I described it earlier.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jemini, yes, but now we lost the house. Could you please mark the house. Could you mark it with an X.

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Very well. And now tell me where the mosque is.

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just approximately here.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And put a number 2 there, please.

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And now the school.

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And a number 3 there, please.

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's not working. Can we have a red pen, please? This won't do. Can we let the witness draw in the junction with a red pen? But if you think it's clear, we can leave it that way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The witness, I'm afraid, can't improve the photograph, and the problem is the photograph does not really depict the junction. I believe the Chamber understands the witness's evidence to be attempting, as near as he can, to mark the location.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I now propose that this exhibit be tendered into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: D00072, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour, and I think it's time for the technical break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It is. We will adjourn now for half an hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. May I have Exhibit P639 put up, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jemini, can you tell me, looking at this opening here, this aperture, what is that?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: You can see the window where I was positioned during the time of war. Opposite to this position you can see a house which is about 12 to 15 metres away, and the balconies of that house, and behind that house there's a third house.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So that is the place where you were on the 25th and the 26th of March, 1999; is that right?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And what about this white house in the distance there? Who does that belong to?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is my house.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So you lived in that house, did you?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I lived to another -- in another house which is a little bit below. It cannot be seen on this photograph. That one was still under construction.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm asking you about this white house. Did anybody use it or not?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So was it a guest house?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The guest house is a little bit further up from this house. This is the third house that was not inhabited and under construction. Below, to the left, is the house where we lived, where we were staying.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So the two houses you just mentioned can't be seen on this photograph. Now, we see a brick building to the right. Was that your house or not?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean the first house with red bricks?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: No, Mr. Jemini. You see the white house and you said that was still under construction, and to the right of that house we can see the roof of another house.

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That is the house of my neighbour. Between these houses is the house that comes as a junction from the main road Gjakova-Prizren, but this house is not related to our family houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So in between that house and the house still under construction there was a wall, was there?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you please repeat your question?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Between your neighbour's house and you there was a wall, was there? Between your two properties. That's what I mean.

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right behind our house there's a wall, but then there is this road which comes as a junction from the main Gjakova-Prizren road. There is a wall, but between the wall of this house and that house there is a road.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell me now, please, looking across the roofs of these houses can you see the school?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: So where is it? Could you mark the school for us.

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot do that on this photograph. You should put up the other photograph that we looked at where the school can be seen.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Just a moment, please. So what you're saying is that you can't see it on this photograph, but can you see the mosque here?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. You cannot see the mosque here either. The mosque can be seen from the other position. The school, however, can be seen from this point of view. There are other photographs where the school can be seen from this position.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We'll come to those photographs. Let's move slowly. Mr. Jemini, did you take this photograph, the one we're looking at now?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. When was this photograph taken?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This photograph was taken upon our return in the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May we now have Exhibit P643 pulled up, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jemini, could you tell us from what point this photograph was taken and what are these houses? Where was the photograph taken from, from what location?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This photograph shows the house where we lived as a family, the house that was burnt down during the war. Then you see the house of my Uncle Jusuf which is about 12 metres further. The photograph was taken from the position where we were hiding, from that window.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So the house without a roof, is that the house you were living in? Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, do you think it would be a good idea to put a number 1 above the house that the witness says was the family house they lived in?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: And the one that was burnt? Yes, it could prevent confusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jemini, above the roof would you place a number 1, please.

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: So number 1 denotes the house you lived in. Now I want to ask you this: Is that the house where your parents and relatives hid in the basement, in the cellar?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And what about the house to the left, the white house with the roof intact? Is that your uncle's house? What was his name again?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. My uncle's son, Isuf, who was with me, or my uncle's house. My uncle's name is Shaip.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Isuf. I see. Thank you. Now would you place a number 2 above Shaip's house?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And what about the house to the right with the yellow wall with no windows? Is that beyond your compound or is that part of your compound?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Between the yellow house and our house is this road that I mentioned so many times. This was the main road coming from the main Prizren-Gjakova road. So this is the road that divides these two houses. So just next to that wall is this small road.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So all the other houses are outside your family holding and beyond the road?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. What I want to ask you now is this: Can you see the school on this photograph?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This is showing the direction toward Zrze village, not to the other part of the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And what about the mosque? Can you see that on this picture?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The school and the mosque are on the opposite direction, to the right. This is the entrance to the village, and they are in the right part of the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, can you see the entrance gate to your compound on this photograph?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Very well. Yes, I understand. Now let me ask you this: When we were looking at the previous photograph and the window where you were at, you couldn't see this house. Am I right in saying that?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: From that window, from this position, you can see this house very well as shown in this photograph, but that was another position. And from that window you could see the house straight before you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jemini, please answer my question. A moment ago we saw a window from which you looked out from. Now, what I'm asking you is this: From the window you were standing at where that first photograph was taken, am I right in saying that you can't see the house which can be seen on this photograph?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: From that position you can see this house, but it's not depicted in that photograph. Something else is depicted on that photograph. But from that position you can see both this house and the direction where these two other houses are. So you can see in three different directions from that position, other position.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jemini, what I'm asking you is this: You took the photograph from your window. Why can't you see this house there? Can you explain that?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand. From this window you can see this house. Why are you saying that you cannot see the house? From this window you can see the house. I don't know if we are understanding each other. If I'm looking straight before me, I will see the Judges. If I look at a different angle, toward my left, then I will see you. If I turn to the right, then I will see the Prosecutor. So from this position you could see from that window this house that was burnt. From another position you can see the two other houses. To the right you could see the mosque and the school. So if you have the photographs from all these different angles, I can point to you the facilities or buildings that you want me to. I think you can tell for yourself that the photograph was taken from a higher position, from a window, that is. In the edge you can see another house, also uninhabited.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Well, I looked carefully but didn't notice that. Now, on the floor you were on, or in the attic space, was there one window or more than one window?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the floor from where we observed, there was only one window. There was another window on the opposite side, but we looked through this window. So there was just this window.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It would help me, Mr. Jemini, to be clear about your evidence. If you could tell, me you marked two photographs on the screen. One of them is shown here, Exhibit P643. You also marked Exhibit P639, a photograph in which your white house, still under construction, was in the centre of the photograph. Those two photographs, were they taken from the same window or from different windows?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They were taken from the same window, Your Honour, from one window through which we observed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: And in this photograph, Exhibit P643, on the extreme right-hand edge of the photograph can be seen a small part of a white house. Is that the white house which is in the centre of the other photograph which you marked?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes, it is the house that we saw in the previous photograph. So from this window you could see the window -- the house in the middle, then the white house. Now, this is another angle from where you can see only this house. So you could see in all these different directions from the same window and take photographs from different angles.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, that has helped the Chamber. Now, Mr. Djurdjic, is there something more you want to proceed with?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Now you've answered, and you told the Judge that you can see the white house under construction. So put a number 3 there, please.

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And now, could you tell me, where is the entrance gate?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: If we go back to the previous photograph, please, then I can show where it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Very well, but can you tell me, since we can't see it, on what side? Just point with your finger, or just describe it. Don't draw anything in yet.

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: You asked me before to point the junction on the main road, Prizren -Gjakova, and the other junction. This is a number 3 marked house where the road turns in the direction of Krusha and in the direction of Bellacerke. Between this white house and the house near my house, there's the gate, the entrance gate, as you turn right from the main road.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, tell me, this plot that is covered in green, how wide is it? In front of your family house.

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think we mentioned it earlier. The wall that you can see from my uncle's house and the whole area there is about 60 acres or 0.6 hectares. It stretches on the surface of 60 to 70 metres on all directions.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So from the window where you were to your family house here, how far is it? What's the distance in metres?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: About 60 or -- 50 or 60 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be -- excuse me. It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, markings made on P00643 would be D00073.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Now I would like us to look at P641.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jemini, could you explain this photograph to us?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This photograph shows straight the position where I was. This is the house, the burnt house, where we lived; and this is the house where we stayed. So the window on the roof, if you want me I can mark it, is the position where we were sheltering.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Now I would like you to mark that spot with X.

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: I assume that's the opening next to the X; right? In the attic. Mr. Jemini, did you hear me?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think there is interpretation. I'm not receiving interpretation. Can you repeat?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Yes. So that's the one. Now we see the white family house. Is this photograph taken from the right-hand side of the building or from an area to the right of the house?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This position is between my cousin's house, Isuf's house, and my house, the one where we were. This is the opposite direction from the previous photograph, depicted in the previous photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: That's quite clear to me, but the lateral area, the lateral part of the house that we can see here; right?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And there's a road behind this house; is that right?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Now tell me, we don't see the other three houses?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: They cannot be seen, because you -- the house that you see here does not allow you to see the other houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And when was this photograph taken?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This photograph was taken after we returned to the village, maybe in September or October 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And now on this photograph we don't see the house where the soldiers were; is that right?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, you cannot see that house. That house is next to -- in the corner where the white house is and the house where we were positioned. You can see that house in the previous photograph, the one we saw first.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We'll go back to that, but you say that between that house and this one where the window is that there was a distance of 10 metres.

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not the house where this -- in this photograph, but the house we were staying in the -- and which was depicted in the previous photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jemini, I said in the house where the soldiers were. You say that the house where the soldiers were and this house were 10 metres apart. Now I'm asking you how is it possible that you cannot see that house? And you can see that there is at least 20 metres -- you can see at least 20 metres from the window.

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The house is about 12 to 15 metres away. I have mentioned it before. It's not more than that, maybe less. However, unfortunately, you cannot see it in this photograph. The distance is not more than 12 to 15 metres. You can see that clearly in the previous photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you make a photograph where all the houses are visible and their disposition, or at least if we could see from two angles, from one spot, all of your family houses?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Unfortunately not. We were not professional photographers. We probably could have taken other photographs that would be clearer and make the position clearer, but we didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And --

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, first of all I would like to tender this photograph into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Markings made on P00641, Your Honours, will be assigned D00074.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could I now have D002-5761 on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jemini, well, now we see a different angle. Is that the same window?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And what can we see from this window?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: From this window you could look at two angles. Now we can see the school in this photograph. The school is in this upper part here. If you want me, I can mark it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Please show it.

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's the one. From this angle, we could see the school when it was burned.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And this house that we can see here, what is it?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The one close to the school?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jemini, this -- what you can see at the left-hand corner of the window, this house that is made of bricks, what is this?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Down here. This is the house that is 12 metres away. This is the house where the commanders of the army were stationed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So you didn't have to pull up the roof tiles in order to be able to see where the school was?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not to see the school, no. To see other things, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. But did you lift the roof tiles at all?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you do that while the army was in this house across the road?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Did you do that while there were guards posted on the floor below you?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And you didn't make any noise, and the guards and the soldiers didn't hear you?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Of course we were stressed and we were at risk all the time, so we were careful all the time and tried to make the least noise possible. So we moved the tiles very little, just to create a little opening from which we could see outside. So we did not remove the tiles altogether. We just moved them a little bit to create an opening in order to be able to see outside.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please look at Defence document D002-5762.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Are you wanting to exhibit this one?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, markings made on D002-5761 will be assigned D00075.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jemini, is this what the attic looked like at the time when you were in there?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to tender this into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document ID D002-5762 will be assigned D00075, Your Honours -- 76, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we please have a document, document -- Defence document D002-5762, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And while we're waiting for the document, Mr. Jemini, all those photographs that we've been looking at were made after your return from Albania. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Djurdjic, the number you last gave is the number of the photograph that's on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I asked for D002-5763, and this was an image of the house. Perhaps I made a mistake. 5762. D002-5763.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jemini, can you tell us what we can see on this photograph?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the house where we used to live.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, this side where we can see this man standing in front of the house, is this the side from which the photograph of the window was taken, the window that you marked with an X?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you please repeat the question?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Yes. Can you see this man standing on the grass in front of the house?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Is he facing the window that you were on in the house where you were in the attic?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. He's facing the opposite side. He is facing the wall and the road which is -- or the alleyway that is behind it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And in relation to this photograph here, where would the house where you were be?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The house would be about 50 or 60 metres away to the opposite way, to the opposite direction, in the direction of Krusha.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Okay. So this man -- this man's back is towards the building where you were.

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Am I right then that the picture, the photograph where we can see the window on the attic where you were, is taken from the side of this building that we can see here but from the other side?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This photograph has been taken by -- from the white house that we did not live in. Ninety degrees compared to the other one.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Very well. Yes, yes. Well, now you've explained this, but am I right if I say that in this family house where you lived, on the other side of it, so it's again the lateral side but the other side, that this is where the photograph of the window in the attic was taken, the one that we have seen just now with the X?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This is a different photograph taken from a different position. It has nothing to do with the position at the house where we were staying at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jemini, please listen to me carefully. It doesn't matter. The photograph was taken from a place where one can see the window where you were standing, the one that you marked with an X. Now I'm asking you, since it is not this side of the house when the previous photograph was taken, so I'm asking you whether it was done from the side but the other side of the building. Is that where the photo was taken from?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please, can I have exhibit -- or, rather, document of the Defence, D002-5759. No, I'm not going to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Do you want this in as an exhibit? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. No thank you, Your Honour. I don't think that we obtained anything. We got an explanation as to where the photograph was taken. That's from the other side, so ... I think that this is actually a document that has already been admitted into evidence as a P exhibit. I'm not sure about the number. I'm sure that it has been admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: This is the place where you rested. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: On the -- do you know when this was taken?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the 5th of April to the 20th of April.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please put an X to show us who you are on this photograph, where you are.

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And this person to the left of you, who is that?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: He's one of the group who was present with us during all the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And do you know his full name?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Xhevdet Ramadani.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And what is it standing against the tree here?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: A automatic rifle.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to tender this into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, markings made on D002-5759 will be assigned D00077.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jemini, in your statement of the 17th of July, you say that up until the 25th of March, 1999, in Celine there were no army and police; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, before the war, did the army and the police ever come to your village?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the last two months, no, but before, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
